claim: When base risk mu exceeds target alpha, any distribution-free conformal risk control method must abstain on at least (mu-alpha)/(1-alpha) of examples -- a closed-form impossibility/feasibility test for whether conformal risk control can succeed before running it.
stance_target: theoretical limits any per-requirement risk-control theorem for code must respect
scope_conditions: structured LLM generation (NER, JSON extraction, QA, classification), 6 open-weight models 3B-72B, 8 datasets, 4 tasks, 6 nonconformity scores
quoted_support: we prove an impossibility result: when the base risk (mu > alpha), any distribution-free method must abstain on at least ((mu-alpha)/(1-alpha)) examples, yielding a closed-form feasibility test

claim: Empirical-Bernstein bounds deliver the largest single gain in certifiable configurations (+37%) over Hoeffding bounds for conformal risk control on structured LLM generation.
stance_target: which statistical bound family a per-requirement risk-control theorem should adopt
quoted_support: the Hoeffding-to-Bernstein step delivers the largest gain (+37% certified configurations), while e-CRC adds value when calibration data is scarce
numbers: 10% certification at 20% data versus 0% for Hoeffding
